sourcedFrom: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page
cleanIntro: The Nylon 66 is a tube-fed .22 Long Rifle autoloader with a stock and receiver of DuPont nylon, a magazine tube that loads through the butt plate, and a safety thumbpiece behind the receiver cover. Remington's care sheet asks for little: the nylon is self-lubricating, so the action needs cleaning only after extended shooting or before storage, and then only a partial take-down — receiver cover off, barrel out of the stock, ejector out — and no further.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, safety thumbpiece back to SAFE
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and push the safety thumbpiece, just behind the receiver cover, rearward to SAFE. On SAFE the red dot behind the thumbpiece is hidden; if you can see red, the rifle is ready to fire.
steps.prose: Remington is plain that the safety only guards against an accidental trigger pull and is no excuse for careless handling — everything after this step still treats the rifle as loaded until you have seen and felt an empty chamber.
steps.quote: Push safety thumbpiece rearward to SAFE position.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — TO UNLOAD, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Magazine tube out through the butt, cartridges out
steps.action: Reach into the recess in the butt plate, turn the magazine plug to unlock the tube and pull the inner magazine tube out of the stock. Turn the muzzle up so the cartridges in the stock run out of the magazine, then put the tube back and turn the plug to lock it.
steps.prose: The magazine lives in the buttstock, not under the barrel, so this is the step people skip when they expect a box magazine. Count what falls out against what you loaded — the tube holds fourteen Long Rifle cartridges.
steps.quote: Unlock and remove magazine tube from rear of stock. Turn muzzle upwards and allow live cartridges to empty from magazine. Replace magazine tube and lock in place.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — TO UNLOAD, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Bolt handle back, repeatedly — then look in the chamber
steps.action: Pull the bolt handle back and let it go, several times, to throw out any cartridge still in the action or the chamber. The colored magazine follower should then show in the ejection port. Look into the chamber through the open ejection port and make sure no cartridge is left in it.
steps.prose: Draw the bolt back and hold it while you look. If a cartridge is jammed in the chamber, do not pry at it: Remington warns that removing a jammed round carries a risk of accidental discharge, and the cure is the take-down in the next steps and a rod from the muzzle, with the muzzle pointed somewhere safe.
steps.quote: Check chamber of barrel from open ejection port to make sure no live cartridge remains in chamber.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — TO UNLOAD — CAUTION, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Cock it, then bolt handle out and receiver cover off
steps.action: With the rifle empty, cock it by pulling the bolt handle back and releasing it. Pull the bolt handle straight out of the bolt. Unscrew and remove the two cover screws, then slide the receiver cover assembly upward and lift it off the rifle.
steps.prose: This is the book's step one, and it is only needed after extended shooting or before storage — Remington says the self-lubricating nylon makes cleaning unnecessary for thousands of rounds. Keep the two cover screws together; they are the only thing holding the cover on.
steps.quote: Unscrew and remove the two (2) cover screws and slide the receiver cover assembly upward and remove from rifle (Fig. 3).
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — Step 1 and ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Barrel lock screw out, barrel bracket up, barrel out of the stock
steps.action: Unscrew the barrel lock screw (part 6 on the exploded view). Lift the barrel bracket (part 4) upward, then slide the barrel out of the stock.
steps.prose: With the barrel free, the bore can be cleaned on the bench and the bolt rails in the stock are open to reach.
steps.quote: Unscrew barrel lock screw (See exploded view page 4, part No. 6). Lift barrel bracket (See exploded view page 4, part No. 4) upward
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — Step 2, instruction sheet, PDF p.4 (exploded view, PDF p.5)

steps.title: Ejector out — and the take-down stops there
steps.action: Remove the ejector from the now-exposed left side of the rifle. That is the whole take-down: put the bolt handle back into the bolt, and go no further.
steps.prose: Remington draws the line here and says so. The bolt, springs, sear and trigger parts stay where they are; the book gives no procedure for them, and a Nylon 66 has many parts that are no longer made.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is required. Replace bolt handle.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: The bore: patch, brush if it needs it, oiled patch last
steps.action: Wipe the bore with a .22 caliber cleaning patch. If it needs more, brush it with a wire brush and powder solvent, then wipe it clean. Finish with a lightly oiled patch.
steps.prose: With the barrel out of the stock this is easy to do from either end. Only brush when patches alone will not lift the fouling.
steps.quote: Use lightly oiled patch after cleaning
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — BARREL CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Bolt back and held: scrape the feed guide and rails, clean the bolt face
steps.action: Pull the bolt assembly back by its handle and hold it there. Scrape the shooting residue from the cartridge feed guide and from the bolt rails in the stock, then clean the face of the bolt.
steps.prose: Scrape, don't flood — the nylon surfaces need no solvent and no oil, and the residue that matters builds up on the feed guide and the rails the bolt rides on.
steps.quote: Scrape shooting residue from cartridge feed guide
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Little or no oil — and none on the nylon
steps.action: Give the metal action parts a very light coat of oil to keep rust off, and leave the nylon parts dry. Wipe the receiver cover and the barrel with an oiled cloth whenever the rifle has been handled, and always after it has been out in wet weather.
steps.prose: Remington says the metal parts work best and stay clean longer with little or no oil. Fingerprints carry moisture that will rust steel, and sudden temperature changes cause condensation, so the wipe-down is what keeps the barrel and cover sound.
steps.quote: The nylon parts need no oil. Use oil sparingly on metallic action parts to prevent rust
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Below freezing: oil off, dry graphite on
steps.action: If you will shoot in below-freezing weather, remove any excess oil from the action and use dry graphite instead.
steps.quote: When shooting in below freezing weather remove any excess oil and use dry graphite.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: Back together in reverse order
steps.action: Refit the ejector, slide the barrel back into the stock, press the barrel bracket down and tighten the barrel lock screw, then set the receiver cover back on and refit its two cover screws.
steps.quote: After cleaning, reassemble parts in reverse order.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4

steps.title: A gunsmith's look, periodically
steps.action: Have the rifle checked by a competent gunsmith from time to time, so worn or damaged parts are found and replaced.
steps.prose: Remington no longer makes the Nylon 66 and says many of its parts may no longer be available. Use only Remington parts, and never alter the trigger, the sear or its notch.
steps.quote: Rifle should be checked periodically by a competent gunsmith to ensure proper inspection and any necessary replacement of worn or damaged parts.
steps.cite: REMINGTON NYLON 66 AUTOLOADING RIFLE 22 CALIBER — Instructions for Operation & Care of Rifle — none printed — a Remington information packet (cover: 'The following documentation represents all information available on this model'); no form number or date on any page — MAINTENANCE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4
steps.warn: DO NOT MAKE CHANGES OR ALTERATIONS TO ANY PARTS OF A FIREARM.

deepAbsentReason: Remington's book ends at the partial take-down it gives for cleaning — receiver cover off, barrel out of the stock, ejector out — and says 'No further disassembly is required' (ACTION CLEANING AND CARE, instruction sheet, PDF p.4). It publishes no deeper procedure, so there is no deep clean for this rifle.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Wipe with a .22 caliber cleaning patch
Wire brush with powder solvent only if needed, then wipe clean
Finish with a lightly oiled patch

cleaning.name: BOLT AND FEED GUIDE
tasks: Bolt assembly pulled back and held
Residue scraped from the cartridge feed guide and the bolt rails in the stock

cleaning.name: METAL PARTS AND STORAGE
tasks: Oil used sparingly on metal action parts only
Do not oil the nylon parts
Receiver cover and barrel wiped with an oiled cloth after handling and after wet weather
Below freezing: excess oil removed, dry graphite used

reassembly: Refit the ejector in the left side of the rifle.
Slide the barrel back into the stock, press the barrel bracket down and tighten the barrel lock screw.
Set the receiver cover assembly back on and refit its two cover screws.
Make sure the bolt handle is fully seated in the bolt.
fncheck: Magazine tube out and the chamber empty. Pull the bolt handle back and release it: the bolt runs back and closes fully under its spring. Push the safety thumbpiece forward and the red dot shows; push it rearward to SAFE and the red dot is hidden. Leave it on SAFE. This check never asks you to pull the trigger.
